slides.title: Click and Grow vs AeroGarden in 2026 — Honest Pick
slides.subtitle: Footprint, noise, pods, and who should buy which for a small kitchen counter.
slides.narration: Click and Grow vs AeroGarden in 2026 — Honest Pick. Here is the practical Sill Garden answer for a small apartment, without buying more equipment than you need.

slides.title: Start with the apartment constraints
bullets: Measure the usable sill, shelf, or counter space
Check daylight before buying a grow light
Protect rental surfaces with trays and saucers
Choose a setup you can maintain every week
slides.narration: Start with your real constraints: usable space, available daylight, water protection, and how much weekly maintenance you will actually do.

slides.title: The simple setup that works
bullets: Use the smallest reliable setup for the job
Put every pot or reservoir on a waterproof tray
Automate light timing before adding more plants
Watch plant response and adjust one thing at a time
slides.narration: Keep the first setup simple. Protect the surface, automate the light schedule, and adjust from what the plants show you instead of changing everything at once.

slides.title: Three expensive mistakes to avoid
bullets: Buying for maximum capacity instead of daily fit
Treating weak light as a watering problem
Ignoring noise, glare, or spill risk in a small room
slides.narration: Avoid buying the largest system first. Weak light is not fixed by extra water, and in a small room noise, glare, and spill risk matter every day.

slides.title: The Sill Garden verdict
slides.body: Choose Click and Grow for simpler quiet setups; AeroGarden when you want more control and capacity.
picks: Start small and prove the routine first
Upgrade light or capacity only when the plants require it
slides.narration: Our verdict: Choose Click and Grow for simpler quiet setups; AeroGarden when you want more control and capacity. Read the full step-by-step guide at Sill Garden dot com.
